description: This donut chart visually compares the distribution of deception outcomes across two levels of ambiguity, labeled “Ambiguity 1 (Outer)” and “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)”, each broken down into three categories: “Deceived” (red), “Partially” (yellow), and “Not Deceived” (green). The outer ring, representing Ambiguity 1, is divided into three segments: the red “Deceived” segment constitutes 67.6% of the outer ring, the yellow “Partially” segment accounts for 31.6%, and the green “Not Deceived” segment makes up 8.8%. The inner ring, representing Ambiguity 2, is similarly divided: the red “Deceived” segment is 57.9%, the yellow “Partially” segment is 23.5%, and the green “Not Deceived” segment is 10.5%. Each segment’s percentage is clearly labeled within its respective area, and the chart includes two legends, one for each ambiguity level, mapping the colors to their corresponding categories. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order, with the largest segment (red) positioned at the top of each ring.
